references.text: Joseph was taken from his land – he was sold by his brothers to the Ishmaelites, who brought him to Egypt. This corresponds to Joseph's words that he was 'stolen away from the land of the Hebrews'.

Joseph was unjustly thrown into prison based on false accusations from Potiphar's wife, even though he had done nothing wrong – as he himself claims: 'nor have I done anything here for which they should put me in the dungeon'.
The psalm describes how Joseph was sold as a slave and put in chains, a poetic summary of his innocent sufferings in Egypt.
In his speech, Stephen refers to the patriarchs selling Joseph into Egypt out of jealousy, which confirms Joseph's statement about being stolen away from the land of the Hebrews.
Contrast between a sinner who feels unfairly treated (Job) and an innocent man who claims his complete righteousness (Joseph).
The hand of the wicked driving the righteous away (Psalm) illuminates Joseph's concrete experience of unjust kidnapping and imprisonment.
